newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle end higher, firm cash.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle end higher, firm cash.

text.p: CME live cattle ended up in response to higher beef cutout values, and feeder cattle ended with sharp gains on firm cash markets, floor traders said.
Big gains in choice grade beef on Thursday was said to have provided most of the fuel for the rally in live catttle, floor traders said.
At midday Friday, USDA again reported gains with beef cut-out values ranging from $0.33 to $1.19 per cwt higher.
Those gains will more than likely pave the way for steady to higher fed cattle prices next week, floor traders and livestock analysts said.
Local traders were long cattle and helped to push the market to daily highs, while commission houses and commercial firms were on both sides of the market.
Some bearish traders argued that an expected seasonal dip in beef demand will drag the market lower, but bullish traders said this year's market was different because of high grain prices.
"We're in a unique situation because of what record-high priced grains did to the (cattle) placement patterns," said one commission house trader.
Supplies of fed cattle remain tight in the near-term, and feedlots are very current, cash-connected sources said.
CME feeder cattle surged near limit-up levels, mostly on strength from cash markets and continued weakness in corn futures, floor traders said.
"As long as corn keeps going down, we're going to keep going up," one feeder cattle trader said.
December live cattle closed up 0.450 at 67.125 cents per lb, and February settled down 0.325 cent at 63.800 cent. Other contracts closed up 0.325 to up 0.500 cent.
November feeder cattle were up 0.90 cent at 64.975 cents a lb, with other contracts up 0.850 to 1.30 cent.
